decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add a bookmark (URL, title, optional description/tags)”; round 1 client did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: The proposed save flow and assignment of tags conform at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed auto-fetching only “page title/favicon”; round 1 client requested “title, description, favicon, and preview image automatically.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the incomplete metadata-fetch scope at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included editable URL/title/description/tags and “Edit”; round 1 client reinforced that fetched metadata must remain editable.
decisions.note: The presented editing decision is consistent with editable bookmark fields; the response reinforces rather than corrects it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly proposed “Edit and delete”; round 1 client did not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Individual bookmark deletion conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed “filter bookmarks by tag”; round 1 client retained tag-oriented search and organization.
decisions.note: Filtering the collection by a selected tag conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered merely a “clean and modern” UI; round 1 client specified “a clean, modern, readability-first look.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing readability-first requirement at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed generic search with no phrase behavior; round 1 client requested strong search “including … exact phrases.”
decisions.note: The client requested the omitted exact-phrase behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed generic search; round 1 client explicitly requested search with “exclusions.”
decisions.note: The client surfaced and requested missing negative-search semantics, although it did not state the reference's complete operator grammar.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted read state; round 1 client requested “read-later status.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing unread/read-later capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted archiving; round 1 client requested “reversible archiving.”
decisions.note: The client added archive behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered deletion but no distinct archive lifecycle; round 1 client requested “reversible archiving.”
decisions.note: Calling for reversibility surfaces the required distinction between archive and permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default contained no note feature; round 1 client requested “notes.”
decisions.note: The client requested the related missing note requirement at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted sorting; round 1 client requested “sorting.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing list-sorting capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted multi-selection actions; round 1 client requested “bulk actions.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing bulk-action capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default did not state duplicate handling; round 1 client said, “Saving the same URL again should open the existing bookmark rather than create a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the reference-conforming duplicate-save rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted reusable filters; round 1 client requested “Saved filter combinations.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing saved-filter/bundle capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted preservation; round 1 client requested “page snapshots.”
decisions.note: The client requested the related missing snapshot requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted import; round 1 client requested “bookmark import/export.”
decisions.note: The client added bookmark import at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted export; round 1 client requested “bookmark import/export.”
decisions.note: The client added bookmark export at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 default omitted user display settings; round 1 client requested “a few display preferences.”
decisions.note: The client requested the related missing display-preference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker said only “search”; the client requested “strong search” but did not identify searchable fields or case handling. Round 2 maker listed operators and said live search worked, but still did not specify title/description/note/URL coverage or case-insensitivity; round 2 client gave general approval.
decisions.note: Across specification and implementation review, the record cannot establish whether full-text field coverage and case-insensitive matching conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Auto-fetch title, description, favicon, preview image … live fetch on paste; all fields editable + re-fetch button”; round 2 client approved the application.
decisions.note: The revised metadata behavior conforms during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented “Read-later status … toggle + dedicated view”; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: A toggle plus dedicated read-later view provides marking unread, viewing unread, and toggling back to read.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented “archive/unarchive with an Undo toast” and an `is:archived` search scope, separately from delete; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation provides reversible archive behavior, distinguishes deletion, and offers an archived-only perspective.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker described notes only as “per-bookmark, shown on cards”; round 2 client gave general approval without discussing markdown.
decisions.note: The implementation review does not establish whether notes accept and render markdown, so divergence cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed sorting by “newest/oldest/recently-updated/title/domain”; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: The implemented sort choices conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “select → read-later, archive, add/remove tag, delete”; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: The presented multi-selection actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker characterized bulk actions solely as “select →” actions and did not present an apply-to-all-current-results operation; round 2 client responded only with general approval.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation omits applying an action to the entire collection matching the current filter; bare approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented tag search using `tag:` rather than the required `#tag` syntax; round 2 client gave only general approval.
decisions.note: The explicit search syntax differs from the reference, and the client did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented “AND terms” and `-exclusions` but no OR, NOT, parenthesized groups, or quoted-literal operator rule; round 2 client gave general approval.
decisions.note: The implemented grammar is materially incomplete relative to the reference; the client's bare approval is not a capture.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly listed `"exact phrases"`; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: Exact-phrase searching conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: re-saving a normalized duplicate “opens the existing bookmark”; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: The required same-URL convergence behavior conforms; extra normalization is not itself a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented saving “query+scope+sort” for one-click reuse; its query syntax includes tag and exclusion filters. Round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: Saving a query that encodes included and excluded tags is functionally equivalent to the reference bundle representation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker described an unqualified per-bookmark process where “Playwright captures full-page PNG + saved HTML”; it did not provide the required PDF-download exception. Round 2 client gave general approval.
decisions.note: The presented universal HTML/PNG snapshot behavior conflicts with storing a PDF target as the PDF itself; the difference was not surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified browser/Netscape HTML import, deduplication, and “folders → tags,” but did not state whether date-added values are preserved; round 2 client gave general approval.
decisions.note: Format and tag handling conform, but the record cannot establish the required date-preservation behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly presented “browser-HTML (Netscape)” export; round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: The export format conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker exhaustively listed “theme, grid/list, density, default sort, show/hide previews” but no font-size control; round 2 client gave general approval.
decisions.note: The implemented preference set omits the reference's font-size adjustment, and bare approval does not show that the client noticed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker described a “clean, readability-first UI” with bookmark cards, fetched metadata, tags, notes, and preview visibility controls; round 2 client said it “looks clean.”
decisions.note: The revised list presentation is consistent with the readability-first requirement.
